problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]x(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: One of the eigenvalues of the matrix is ${\lambda }_{1}=-2+\text{i}.$*
worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].$ 

We are given that the eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-2+\text{i}.$ 

Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors. For ${\lambda }_{1}=-2+\text{i},$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}-\text{i} & -1 \\ 1 & -\text{i}\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\text{i} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=-2+\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{(-2+\text{i})t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{(-2+\text{i})t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\text{i}{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ {e}^{-2t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\text{i}{e}^{-2t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t} \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{2}$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & =2[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}-[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$
